mainTopic: Which property transfers return in יובל: the בכור, a husband who inherits his wife, a יבם, and a gift
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous משנה's limits on the בכור's double portion. He gets no double share in growth that happens by itself, and none in the grandfather's estate, which counts as ראוי. A new משנה then lists transfers that do not return in יובל: the בכור's share, a husband who inherits his wife, and a יבם. רבי מאיר adds a gift to the list, and the חכמים say a gift is like a sale. רבי אלעזר says all of them return, and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says the husband returns his wife's land and deducts money. The גמרא explains each view by sorting the cases into 'gift' or 'inheritance,' using ״לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם״ and the extra word ״תָּשׁוּבוּ״. Next comes רבי יוחנן's rule that brothers who divide an estate are like buyers. רב הושעיא challenges it, and the גמרא debates whether 'returning' means the בכור loses his share for nothing. Finally, the גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה is talking about a family graveyard, returned to avoid פגם משפחה, minus the value of the wife's grave. The chapter יש בכור then closes.

steps.title: The repeated rule about growth includes growth that happens by itself
steps.stepSummary: The repeated phrase 'not in שבח' teaches that even growth that happens on its own, with no work done, is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule is repeated to include an increase in value that happens by itself, such as unripe grain that became full ears, or date blossoms that became dates.
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier, the גמרא asked why the משנה repeats 'they do not take in שבח'. Here it answers that the repetition adds a new case: growth that happens on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the בכור is excluded only from growth that came from his brothers' work after the father died. The extra words teach that he is excluded even when the produce simply ripened by itself. The reason is that this value still did not exist when the father died.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to add a case
Growth in value that happens by itself
Green, unripe grain (fodder)
Full ears of grain
Date blossoms or unripe dates

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'growth by itself' already belonged to the father. The point is the opposite: even this kind of growth counts as new value that came after his death.

phrases.english: To include an enhancement that comes by itself:
phrases.notes: Answers the earlier question of why the משנה repeats this rule

phrases.english: unripe grain that became full ears,
date blossoms that became dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier about why the משנה repeats the rule
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repetition of 'not in שבח' includes growth that happens naturally, without anyone's work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה repeat 'not in שבח'?

steps.title: The repeated rule about due property includes the grandfather's estate
steps.stepSummary: The repeated phrase 'not in ראוי as in מוחזק' teaches that property due from the grandfather is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the repetition of 'not in what is due as in what is held' comes to include the property of the father's father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second repeated phrase. It adds the case of the grandfather's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the father dies before the grandfather. When the grandfather later dies, his estate passes through the father to the sons. Even though this property was sure to come, the father never actually held it. So it counts as ראוי, and the בכור takes no double portion in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that is due to come in but is not yet held
Property already in one's possession
The grandfather's property

steps.whatToRemember: The בכור's double portion covers only what the father actually held at his death. It does not cover later growth, even natural growth, and it does not cover property that was only due to him, such as the grandfather's estate.

phrases.english: And 'not in what is due as in what is held,'
comes to include the property of the father's father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel answer for the second repeated phrase
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repetition of 'not in ראוי' includes the grandfather's estate when the father died before the grandfather.

steps.title: New משנה: inheritances that do not return in יובל
steps.stepSummary: The בכור's extra portion, a husband's inheritance from his wife, and a יבם's inheritance from his brother do not return in יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: These do not return in the יובל year: the בכור's portion, a man who inherits his wife, and a man who does יבום with his brother's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three kinds of transfers that stay with the new owner even after יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יובל, a sold field goes back to its original family, but these transfers are not sales. The גמרא will explain that רבי מאיר, whose list this is, treats the בכור's extra share and the יבם's share as a gift (Steps 9–10) and the husband's share as an inheritance. For him, neither a gift nor an inheritance returns, so the land stays with whoever received it.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation of מתניתין; the משנה
The fiftieth year, when sold fields return to their owners
They return
The firstborn's right to a double portion
One who marries his childless brother's widow (יבום)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'return' does not mean giving the land back to the person who died. It means giving it back to the other heirs or to the original family. The בכור, for example, does not have to put his extra portion back to be divided among his brothers.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these do not return in the Jubilee:
the firstborn's portion, and one who inherits his wife,
and one who does levirate marriage with his brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור's portion, a husband's inheritance from his wife, and a יבם's inheritance do not return in יובל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the main principle: inheritance is permanent, while a sale returns in יובל.

steps.title: Dispute about whether a gift returns in יובל
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a gift does not return. The חכמים say a gift is like a sale, so it does return.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a gift also does not return, according to רבי מאיר. The חכמים say a gift is like a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a gift to the list, but only according to רבי מאיר. The חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats a gift like inheritance, so it stays with the receiver for good. The חכמים treat it like a sale, since it is a voluntary transfer between people, so it returns to the giver in יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift
A sale
The תנא who says a gift stays permanently
The majority of the Sages

phrases.english: And a gift, according to Rabbi Meir;
and the Rabbis say: a gift is like a sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disputed fourth case to the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר a gift does not return. According to the חכמים it returns, like a sale.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: all of these return in יובל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר holds that every case on the list returns in יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: all of them return in the יובל year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with the whole list. He says all of these transfers go back in יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a sharp disagreement with the first opinion in the משנה. The גמרא will later explain what רבי אלעזר means and what his reasoning is.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who says all of them return
All of them

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּם חוֹזְרִין בַּיּוֹבֵל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: All of them return in the Jubilee.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּם חוֹזְרִין בַּיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the opening list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed transfers return in יובל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: the husband returns his wife's land and deducts its value
steps.stepSummary: A husband who inherits his wife must return the land to her family, but he takes its value from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: even a man who inherits his wife must return the land to her family members, and he deducts the money from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה gives a special rule for the husband who inherits his wife. The land goes back to her family, but the husband gets paid for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land goes back to the wife's family, but the husband does not lose out, because he collects its value from them. This combination looks strange. Steps 24–28 explain that the case is a family graveyard, and that the 'deduction' is the value of his wife's grave.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא with the middle-ground view
The members of her family
And he deducts
Money; the value

steps.whatToRemember: Opinions in this משנה: (1) The listed inheritances stay permanently. (2) A gift is disputed: רבי מאיר says it stays, and the חכמים say it is like a sale. (3) רבי אלעזר says all of them return. (4) רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says the husband returns his wife's land but is paid its value.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:
even one who inherits his wife
must return it to the members of the family,
and he deducts from them the money.
phrases.notes: Step 28 explains what this deduction is.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַיּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third approach, limited to the husband's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband returns his wife's inherited land to her family and collects its value from them.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר say these cases do not return?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source and logic behind רבי מאיר's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by asking why רבי מאיר holds that none of the cases on the list return in יובל. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said that even a gift does not return in יובל. The גמרא wants the Torah basis for this, and it also wants to know how each case on the list fits into it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The תנא who holds that a gift does not return in יובל
The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the dispute that was stated in the משנה (Step 4).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source and logic for רבי מאיר's view that these cases do not return in יובל.

steps.title: Only a sale returns; gifts and inheritances do not
steps.stepSummary: The Torah only says that a sale returns in יובל. Gifts and inheritances do not. Each case on the list gets the status of whichever category it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah said that a sale should return in יובל. A gift and an inheritance do not. Cases that come from inheritance count as inheritance, and cases that come from a gift count as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי מאיר. The Torah's rule of returning in יובל is about a sale only. It then says that each case on the list will be sorted as either inheritance or gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the verse narrowly: it talks about land that was sold, so only a sale goes back. That leaves two groups that stay with their owners, gifts and inheritances. The last line sets up a sorting task, and the next steps place each case into one of these two groups.

keyTerms.meaning: Sale
Gift
Inheritance
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
The Jubilee year, when sold land goes back to its original family

phrases.english: It is a sale about which the Merciful One said
it should return in the Jubilee,
but a gift and an inheritance do not.
And these that come from inheritance are inheritance,
and those from a gift are a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶכֶר הוּא דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא לֶיהְדַּר בַּיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah's rule of returning applies only to a sale. Gifts and inheritances stay with the owner, and each case on the list takes the status of its category.

steps.title: The firstborn's double portion is called a gift
steps.stepSummary: The Torah uses the word 'to give' for the בכור's double portion, so it counts as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a בכור, the verse says 'to give him a double portion.' The Torah calls it a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places the first case, the בכור, into the gift group. It proves this from the Torah's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says ״לָתֶת״, 'to give.' That wording shows the extra share is treated as a gift, not plain inheritance. Since רבי מאיר holds that a gift does not return, the בכור's extra share stays with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son, who receives a double share
A double portion
To give, the word that marks it as a gift
Called it

phrases.english: A firstborn: 'to give him a double portion'
the Merciful One called it a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the gift category from Step 8 to the בכור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור's extra share is a gift, because the Torah says 'to give,' so for רבי מאיר it does not return.

steps.title: Husband and יבם count as heirs
steps.stepSummary: A husband's inheritance from his wife comes from Torah law. The Torah calls the יבם a בכור. So both are outside the rule of returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who inherits his wife: a husband's inheritance is from the Torah. One who marries his brother's widow: the Torah calls him 'firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places the last two cases on the list. The husband is a true Torah heir. The יבם is called a בכור, so he gets the same treatment as the firstborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל is from the Torah, it is a real inheritance, and inheritance does not return. The יבם is linked to the בכור through the verse ״וְהָיָה הַבְּכוֹר״, so he gets the same result as the בכור in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's inheritance of his wife's property
From Torah law
One who performs levirate marriage (יבום)
His brother's wife

steps.confusionAlert: The יבם is not actually a firstborn. The Torah's verse simply calls him 'בכור', and that label is enough to give his share the same law as a firstborn's portion.

phrases.english: And one who inherits his wife:
the inheritance of a husband is by Torah law;
and one who performs levirate marriage with his brother's wife:
the Merciful One called him 'firstborn.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes sorting the cases on the list for רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband is a Torah heir, and the יבם is treated like a בכור. Neither returns the land in יובל.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים treat a gift like a sale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים' view that a gift is like a sale and asks for their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: a gift is like a sale. What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the dispute. It quotes the חכמים and asks how they know a gift returns. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that רבי מאיר limits the verse to a sale. So the חכמים need a Torah source that adds gifts to the rule of returning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view
A gift is like a sale
The Rabbis, the same as the חכמים

phrases.english: And the Sages say: a gift is like a sale.
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's reasoning to the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the חכמים' view that a gift returns in יובל.

steps.title: The extra word 'you shall return' includes a gift
steps.stepSummary: The Torah repeats the word ״תָּשׁוּבוּ״, and the extra word comes to add a gift to the rule of returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall return' comes to include a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים learn from an extra word in the Torah that a gift also returns in יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already said 'you shall return' (ויקרא כ״ה:י׳), and it says it again (ויקרא כ״ה:י״ג). The חכמים use this extra word as a רבוי, an inclusion, so a gift is added to a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall return
To include, from an extra word in the verse

phrases.english: 'You shall return'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:13, repeating the same word from 25:10.

phrases.english: comes to include a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word ״תָּשׁוּבוּ״ includes a gift in the rule of returning.

steps.title: For the חכמים, all the listed cases are inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים also hold that the cases on the list do not return, because they treat all of them as inheritance, not gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are all inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חכמים still agree that the listed cases do not return. They see all of them as inheritance, and inheritance does not return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר called the בכור's share a 'gift.' The חכמים, who hold that gifts do return, must treat it as inheritance instead. They agree that the husband and the יבם are also heirs. So both sides reach the same result for this list, but for different reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
They are

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: only a sale returns, and the listed cases are gift or inheritance, so they stay. חכמים: a gift also returns (from ״תָּשׁוּבוּ״), but all the listed cases are inheritance, so they stay too.

phrases.english: And these are all inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the חכמים, who say gifts return, still agree that the listed cases do not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the חכמים, the בכור's portion, the husband's inheritance, and the יבם's share are all inheritance, so they do not return in יובל.

steps.title: The חכמים read the בכור's extra share as inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים compare the בכור's extra share to his regular share. Since the regular share is an inheritance, the extra share is an inheritance too.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the firstborn, the verse says: 'to give him a double portion.' The verse compares the firstborn's extra share to a regular brother's share. Just as the regular share is an inheritance, the firstborn's extra share is also an inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the חכמים' view from step 13. It shows how the חכמים read the בכור's verse so that his share counts as inheritance, not gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר read the word 'to give' as proof that the בכור's share is a gift. The חכמים read the same verse differently. The phrase 'double portion' links the extra share to the regular share, so both share the same legal status. Since inheritance does not return in the יובל, the בכור's share also stays with him.

keyTerms.meaning: A double portion, the בכור's share
Compares (a היקש), linking two things so they share the same law
A regular brother's share
The firstborn's extra share

steps.confusionAlert: The same verse, 'to give him a double portion,' is used by both sides. רבי מאיר stresses the word 'to give' and calls it a gift. The חכמים stress the comparison to the regular share and call it inheritance.

phrases.english: A firstborn: the verse says:
'To give him a double portion,'
it compares the firstborn's share to a regular share.
Just as a regular share is inheritance,
so too the firstborn's share is inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוֹר אָמַר קְרָא: לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם, מַקִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse-based reason behind step 13's claim that the חכמים treat the בכור's share as inheritance.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש between the extra share and the regular share makes the בכור's extra share an inheritance, so it does not return in the יובל.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אלעזר: all these lands return
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's opinion from the משנה that all the listed cases return in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: All of them return in the יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next opinion in the משנה. This is a setup line, and the next step will explain רבי אלעזר's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed cases that do not return in the יובל: the בכור, a husband who inherits his wife, and a יבם. רבי אלעזר disagrees with the whole list and says every one of them returns.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the list in the משנה
Return to the original owners in the יובל year

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
All of them return in the Jubilee.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּם חוֹזְרִים בַּיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חכמים to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every case on the משנה's list returns in the יובל.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר agrees a gift returns and treats every case as a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר holds like the חכמים that 'תָּשׁוּבוּ' includes a gift. He also holds that all the listed cases are gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the חכמים, who say 'you shall return' comes to include a gift. And all of these cases are gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר says everything returns. It combines two ideas: a gift returns in the יובל, and every case on the list is a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר agrees with the חכמים on the first point, that a gift returns (step 12). He disagrees with them on the second point. The חכמים called these cases inheritance (step 13), but רבי אלעזר calls them gifts. So they return.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (the view of)
To include, to add something to a rule
A gift

phrases.english: He holds like the Rabbis, who say:
'You shall return' comes to include a gift,
and these are all gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A gift returns in the יובל, and all the listed cases count as gifts.

steps.title: Why the firstborn's share counts as a gift for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The Torah uses the word 'to give' for the בכור, so רבי אלעזר treats his share as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn: 'to give him a double portion.' The Torah calls it a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes case by case to show why each one is a gift for רבי אלעזר. It starts with the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אלעזר reads the verse like רבי מאיר did in step 9. The word 'to give' makes the share a gift. Unlike רבי מאיר, though, רבי אלעזר holds that gifts return in the יובל, so the בכור's share returns.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') called it
To give, the word that signals a gift

phrases.english: A firstborn: 'to give him a double portion,'
the Merciful One called it a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוֹר — לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם, מַתָּנָה קַרְיֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts proving step 16's claim that every case is a gift, beginning with the בכור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'to give' makes the בכור's share a gift, so it returns in the יובל.

steps.title: The husband and the יבם also return
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אלעזר, a husband's inheritance from his wife is only rabbinic law. The יבם is called a בכור, so his share is like a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who inherits his wife: a husband's inheritance is rabbinic law. One who marries his brother's widow: the Torah calls him a 'firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list. It shows why the husband and the יבם also return their land, according to רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, the husband's inheritance was treated as Torah law. רבי אלעזר holds it is only rabbinic law, so by Torah law it is not a true inheritance and the land returns. The יבם is called a בכור in the Torah. Since רבי אלעזר holds the בכור's share is a gift (step 17), the יבם's share returns too.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's inheritance of his wife's property
From rabbinic law, not Torah law
One who does יבום, marrying his brother's childless widow

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: a gift returns, and all three cases count as gifts or are not true Torah inheritance. בכור = 'to give'. Husband = rabbinic inheritance only. יבם = called a בכור. So all of them return in the יובל.

phrases.english: And one who inherits his wife:
a husband's inheritance is by rabbinic law;
and one who marries his brother's wife in levirate marriage:
the Merciful One called him a 'firstborn.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ — יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the case-by-case explanation that began with the בכור in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband's inheritance is only rabbinic, and the יבם is called a בכור, so both return in the יובל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי אלעזר, none of the listed cases is a true Torah inheritance, so all of them return in the יובל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: brothers who divided an estate are like buyers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that brothers who split an inheritance count as buyers from each other. So they must return their shares in the יובל and divide again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Brothers who divided an estate are buyers, and they return the land to each other in the יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ruling of רבי יוחנן about brothers who split their father's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not say each brother received exactly the piece that was 'his' from the start. Instead, each brother is seen as having bought his piece from the others. Bought land returns in the יובל, so the brothers give back their shares and divide the land again.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who divided (an inheritance)
Buyers, purchasers
The אמורא whose ruling is quoted by רבי אסי

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge. If every divided share counts as bought, the בכור's share should also return, and that clashes with the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Brothers who divided are purchasers,
and they return to each other in the Jubilee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ לָקוֹחוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the explanation of the משנה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who divide an inheritance are like buyers, and they must return the land to each other in the יובל.

steps.title: רב הושעיא challenges from the בכור in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא objects from the משנה, which says the בכור's share does not return in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא challenged: 'And these do not return in the יובל: the firstborn's share!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling using the משנה. The משנה clearly says the בכור's share stays and does not return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If brothers who divide are buyers, then every share, including the בכור's, was 'bought' and should return in the יובל. But the משנה lists the בכור's share among the things that do not return. So the משנה seems to treat divided inheritance as true inheritance, not as a purchase.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection
The אמורא who raises the challenge
The firstborn's right and share

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya raised an objection:
'And these are what do not return in the Jubilee:
the firstborn's share!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that brothers who divide are buyers who return the land in the יובל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the brothers are buyers, the בכור's share should return too. The משנה says it does not, so divided inheritance must count as inheritance and not as a purchase.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains 'They do not return'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers רב הושעיא. When the משנה says the בכור's share 'does not return,' it means the בכור does not lose his double portion when the brothers divide again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: What does 'they do not return' mean? They do not return for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers רב הושעיא's question from the משנה by reading the words 'אין חוזרין' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הושעיא thought the משנה meant the בכור's land never goes back into the shared pool in the יובל. That would contradict רבי יוחנן, who said brothers act as buyers from each other and must re-split. רבי אלעזר says all the land does return and get divided again, but the בכור is not left empty-handed. He gets his double portion again in the new division.

keyTerms.meaning: they do not return (in the יובל)
for nothing; as a total loss

steps.confusionAlert: Under this reading, 'they do not return' does NOT mean the land stays put. The land still goes back to be divided again. The phrase only means the בכור does not lose his extra share.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to him:
What does 'they do not return' mean?
They do not return for nothing.
phrases.notes: The בכור gets his double portion again in the new division.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי ״אֵין חוֹזְרִין״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הושעיא's objection from Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור's share never goes back in the יובל, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the land returns and is divided again, but the בכור is not cheated of his double portion.

steps.title: רב ששת questions the implication
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects. If 'they do not return' means 'not for nothing,' then the view that says 'they return' would mean the בכור loses his share for nothing. Who would say that?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects to this: By implication, does the one who says 'they return' mean that they return for nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רבי אלעזר's reading by looking at what it implies about the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אין חוזרין' means 'not lost for nothing,' then the other side, 'חוזרין,' must mean 'lost for nothing.' רב ששת finds it hard to believe that anyone would take away a בכור's Torah-given double portion for no reason. So he doubts רבי אלעזר's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: objects to it; strongly challenges it
by implication; it follows that

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objects to it:
By implication, the one who says 'they return'
is saying they return for nothing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's reading from Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading of 'אין חוזרין' as 'not lost for nothing'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading forces the opposing view to say the בכור loses his share for nothing, which seems unreasonable.

steps.title: רב חמא: there is such a view
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא applies a verse to רב ששת: knowing ברייתות is not enough without the teachings of the אמוראים. He cites רבין's tradition that 'they return' really does mean 'they return for nothing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא read about רב ששת: 'Wisdom is good with an inheritance.' Didn't they hear what רבין said when he came? He said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי אלעזר said it in the name of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע: What does 'they return' mean? They return for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא defends רבי אלעזר's reading against רב ששת. He shows that a known tradition says the 'they return' view does mean the share is lost for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse hints that רב ששת 'inherited' a lot of ברייתות but missed this tradition from the אמוראים. רבין reported, in the name of רבי יוחנן (or, by another version, רבי אלעזר in the name of the תנא רבי אלעזר בן שמוע), that 'they return' means 'they return for nothing.' So the implication רב ששת found strange is in fact an accepted opinion. רבי אלעזר's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Wisdom is good with an inheritance' (קהלת ז:יא)
when רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
and some say (another version of who said it)

steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that the debate in the משנה is real. One side protects the בכור's double portion, and the other side says it is lost in the יובל.

phrases.aramaic: קָרֵי רַב חָמָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Chama read about Rav Sheshet:
'Wisdom is good with an inheritance'
phrases.notes: Inherited knowledge of ברייתות needs the wisdom of the אמוראים too.

phrases.english: and didn't they hear this

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אָתֵי רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: that when Ravin came, he said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,
and some say Rabbi Elazar said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua:
What does 'they return' mean?
They return for nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי רַב חָמָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's objection from Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a received tradition that confirms the implication
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one would say the בכור loses his share for nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע does say that, so רבי אלעזר's reading is fine.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: a husband who inherits his wife must give the land back to her family. It then asks a two-sided question. Either way he holds, his ruling seems not to make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: Even one who inherits his wife must return the land to the members of her family, and so on. What does he hold? If he holds a husband's inheritance is from the Torah, why must he return it to the family? And if he holds it is only rabbinic, why does he get money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה. It sets up a dilemma about רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's ruling, preparing for the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a husband inherits by Torah law, the land is truly his and should not go back in the יובל. If he inherits only by rabbinic law, the land really belongs to her family, so they should not have to pay him. Either way, his ruling (return the land but receive its value) seems contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: a husband's inheritance of his wife's property
from the Torah
from the Rabbis
money; the land's value

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
even one who inherits his wife
must return it to the members of (her family), etc.
What does he hold?
If he holds a husband's inheritance is from the Torah
why must he return it to the family members?
And if he holds a husband's inheritance is rabbinic
what is the money for?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that a husband's inheritance is from the Torah or rabbinic, given that neither fits his ruling.

steps.title: The case of the family graveyard
steps.stepSummary: He holds a husband's inheritance is from the Torah. The case is a family graveyard. To avoid shame to her family, the Rabbis said he takes money and gives it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, he holds that a husband's inheritance is from the Torah. What are we dealing with here? A case where his wife left him her family's graveyard. Because of the family's shame, the Rabbis said he should take money and return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma. It narrows the case to a special situation: a family burial ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the land truly belongs to the husband, which is why he is paid for it. But it would shame her family to bury their dead in land owned by an outsider. So the Rabbis made him sell it back at its value. This is a special exception, not a change in the basic rule that the husband inherits by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: actually; really (keeping the first option)
what case are we dealing with here?
graveyard; burial ground
shame to the family

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds a husband's inheritance is from the Torah. His 'return it for money' ruling applies only to a family graveyard, because of family shame.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a rabbinic enactment can change how a Torah-level ownership plays out, while the ownership itself stays in place.

phrases.english: Actually, he holds a husband's inheritance is from the Torah,
and what are we dealing with here?
such as where his wife left him a graveyard,
and because of family shame the Rabbis said:
he should take money and return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma raised in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He holds a husband inherits by Torah law. The ruling applies to a family graveyard, where the Rabbis required selling it back to prevent family shame.

steps.title: A family can bury a relative in a grave he sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the idea from Step 25 that the Rabbis protect a family from shame when it comes to graves.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If a man sells his grave, the path to his grave, the place where people stand to comfort mourners, or the place for his eulogy, his family members may come and bury him there even against the buyer's wishes. This is because of the shame to the family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for its answer in Step 25. The answer was that the Rabbis made the husband return the family graveyard so the wife's family would not be shamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a sale of burial property is overridden so the family is not shamed. Their relative should not be buried somewhere else. This shows that פגם משפחה is a real concern for the Rabbis. That makes it reasonable that they would make a husband return a family graveyard he inherited.

keyTerms.meaning: And as a ברייתא teaches. It brings an outside source in support.
His grave
The place where people stand to comfort the mourners
The place where his eulogy is given
Against his will. Here it means against the buyer's wishes.
A flaw or shame to the family's honor

steps.confusionAlert: The family buries the man who sold the grave, and the buyer's wishes are what is overridden. The phrase בעל כרחו refers to the buyer, not the dead man.

phrases.english: And as it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who sells his grave, or the path to his grave,
the place where people stand to comfort mourners, or the place of his eulogy —
the family members come and bury him there
against the buyer's will,
because of the shame to the family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 25, that the reason is to avoid shame to the family.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the Rabbis override normal ownership of burial land to prevent פגם משפחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about someone who sold his grave and burial-related areas

steps.title: What does 'he deducts from the money' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase from רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's teaching means: 'he deducts for them from the money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is meant by 'he deducts for them from the money'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the last part of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's statement. The husband gives back the land for money, so what amount is he supposed to subtract? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 explained that the husband returns the family graveyard and is paid for it. But the teaching also says he deducts something from the payment. The גמרא now wants to know what that deduction is.

keyTerms.meaning: He deducts or subtracts
The money, meaning the payment or price

phrases.english: And what is meant by
'he deducts for them from the money'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a remaining phrase in רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's ruling to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What amount the husband subtracts from the payment he receives for returning the land

steps.title: He subtracts the cost of his wife's grave
steps.stepSummary: The deduction is the value of his wife's grave, since a husband must pay for his wife's burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the value of his wife's grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the husband subtracts the value of his wife's grave from the payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband is obligated to bury his wife at his own cost. She was buried in her family's graveyard, so he did not have to pay for a grave. That is why the value of her grave comes off the money the family pays him for the land.

keyTerms.meaning: The value of a grave
His wife

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, a husband really does inherit his wife from the Torah. But when the property is a family graveyard, the Rabbis made him return it for money to avoid פגם משפחה. He subtracts the value of his wife's grave, because her burial was his responsibility.

phrases.english: The value of his wife's grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deduction is the value of the wife's grave, since the husband is obligated to pay for her burial.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק יש בכור
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter יש בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, יש בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line that marks the end of the chapter יש בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows love for the learning and a hope to come back and review it. It is not a legal statement. It simply marks that the chapter is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said at the end of a chapter.
The name of the chapter, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter יש בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the sugya has finished.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter יש בכור is complete.
